findings.evidence: Lines 67–75 declare both definitions without finiteness; `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Basic.lean:229-232` computes tuple height using real `⨆`, while `Real.iSup_of_not_bddAbove` makes an unbounded supremum `0`. The roadmap signature at `Suggested.lean:1469-1471` explicitly requires `[Finite m] [Finite n]`.
findings.fix: Require `[Finite m] [Finite n]` on both definitions and propagate those assumptions through their API, as in the roadmap signature.
findings.issue: `mulHeight` and `logHeight` accept infinite row and column types, although the intended object is the height of a finite entry tuple. For an unbounded infinite tuple (for example rational entries indexed by `ℕ`), `Real.iSup` at the archimedean absolute value is the conditionally-complete-lattice junk value `0`, so a nonzero matrix can have `mulHeight = 0` and `logHeight = 0`.

summary: The public definitions omit the finiteness assumptions required for entry height, exposing degenerate values on infinite matrices.
